text:
Alex R: Quick UX review request — compact pool card: min/max stepper, burst pill, and SLO slider guardrail tooltips. Trying to finalize before tomorrow's handoff.
Priya S: Love it. Main question: do we keep burst as a toggle + pill or a separate inline control? small screens are tight.
Jordan T: If we keep it inline we need to preserve clear affordance that burst is temporary and not part of baseline capacity. Also need to show cost impact.
Samira K: From infra: burst is a different scheduling class. We should avoid using same numeric control for burst and min/max to prevent accidental commits.
Marco L: Suggestion: keep min/max stepper as primary, then a subtle "Add burst" CTA that expands into a compact row with a pill and a tiny numeric stepper. Visual hierarchy keeps baseline first.
Alex R: That matches my thought. What about keyboard flow? tab order should be min -> max -> add-burst -> burst-stepper.
Maria N: A11y: ensure each control has an explicit aria-label. e.g., aria-label="Minimum capacity (GPUs)". Also contrast: the burst pill text is currently 3.2:1, needs 4.5:1.
Priya S: Good catch Maria. For copy on the burst CTA: alternatives: "Add burst capacity", "Enable burst", "Temporary burst". Which is clearest?
Jordan T: "Add burst capacity" is explicit. But on hover we should show a tooltip: "Temporary extra GPUs for traffic spikes — billed per minute."
Samira K: Implementation note: backend accepts burst_quanta param; UI should show human-friendly units. Avoid exposing quanta numbers.
Marco L: UX microcopy proposal (short): Primary label: "Capacity"; min input label: "Min"; max input label: "Max"; small helper: "Expected steady-state range". Burst CTA: "Add burst capacity" and pill label: "+{n} burst (temp)"
Alex R: Love the short labels — fits compact layout. Can we add a faint badge to indicate if pool is preemptible? e.g., "preemptible" badge next to pool name.
Samira K: Yes, we have that flag. Should the badge be a toggle in the card or read-only?
Marco L: Read-only — it's a property of the pool. For accessibility, include title attribute: "This pool uses preemptible instances; capacity may be reclaimed."
Maria N: Also keyboard: burst expand must be reachable and not hidden behind a hover. Use aria-expanded on the CTA. When expanded, set focus to the burst value input.
Priya S: UX nit: the SLO slider guardrail currently overlays the cost preview and obscures numbers on small widths. We should move the guardrail tooltip to anchor below the slider with a subtle chevron and avoid overlap.
Jordan T: Agree. Also add an inline "why" link that opens a small modal explaining guardrail behavior vs SLO.
Alex R: Can someone paste final microcopy suggestions? I'll push to figma after updates.
Marco L: Final microcopy (compact):
- Capacity header: "Capacity"
- Min label (aria-label): "Minimum capacity (GPUs)"
- Max label (aria-label): "Maximum capacity (GPUs)"
- Burst CTA: "Add burst capacity" (button)
- Burst pill: "+{n} burst (temporary)"
- Guardrail tooltip short: "SLO guardrail: keeps latency within target by capping autoscale. Learn more."
- Cost preview label: "Estimated cost / hr"
Maria N: Accessibility checklist for this card: list items as strings so devs can check quickly: "1) all controls have aria-labels", "2) visible focus styles for stepper and pill", "3) contrast >= 4.5:1 for text", "4) screen reader order matches visual order", "5) aria-expanded on burst CTA"
Samira K: Quick dev notes: API fields to update: "min_capacity", "max_capacity", "burst_capacity", "burst_ttl_seconds". We'll map burst TTL to human friendly label on UI.
Priya S: One more copy tweak: change "SLO guardrail" to "SLO guardrail (beta)" only if feature not GA. Otherwise just "SLO guardrail".
Alex R: Thanks all — I'll update figma and ping design-review thread when ready.
UXBot: Reminder: accessibility checklist template updated: https://go/redwood/a11y-checklist (auto-post)
